mainTopic: The end of the Torah-and-water discussion, then the greatness of rain and the sins that cause rain to be held back, with their remedy of prayer
overview: This amud finishes the story of רבי יהושע and בת קיסר. It also gives a second reason why Torah is compared to water, wine and milk: they spoil only through carelessness, and Torah is forgotten only through הסח הדעת. The גמרא then turns to rain. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says a day of rain is as great as the day of creation, and רב אושעיא says salvation grows on it. רבי תנחום בר חנילאי says rain falls only when ישראל's sins are forgiven. Then a long list follows of sins that cause rain to be held back: deserving destruction, neglecting תרומות ומעשרות, לשון הרע, עזות פנים, ביטול תורה, and גזל. Along the way, several אמוראים discuss how bad brazenness is. A brazen person sins, may be called a רשע, and may even be hated. רבי אמי teaches that the remedy for withheld rain is more prayer and strong prayer for mercy, though right behavior from the start is better. The amud ends as ריש לקיש begins a different reading of 'אם קהה הברזל' about a תלמיד, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהושע answers: the beautiful ones would be even wiser if they were ugly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers בת קיסר's objection by saying that beautiful scholars would have been even greater if they were not beautiful.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were ugly, they would be even more learned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers בת קיסר's challenge, which came on the previous amud. She asked: aren't there beautiful people who are also wise?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע had taught that Torah stays best in a plain vessel, the way wine keeps best in simple clay jars. She objected that some good-looking people are learned. He does not deny it, but says their good looks still cost them something: without that beauty they would have learned even more.

phrases.english: If they had been ugly —
phrases.notes: Refers to the beautiful scholars she pointed to.

phrases.english: they would have been even more learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲווֹ סְנוּ טְפֵי הֲווֹ גְּמִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story earlier and answers בת קיסר's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the facts but reframes them: beauty still lowers how much a scholar learns.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Beautiful scholars seem to show that a fine vessel does not hurt Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: Beauty still holds them back. Plainness would have made them even greater.

steps.title: Second reason: liquids and Torah are lost only through carelessness
steps.stepSummary: Another reason for comparing Torah to water, wine and milk: these liquids spoil only when left unwatched, and Torah is forgotten only when it is not reviewed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: just as these three liquids spoil only when people stop paying attention to them, so too Torah is forgotten only when people stop paying attention to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate reason why תורה is compared to water, wine and milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason was about the vessel: humility and plainness. This reason is about guarding. A liquid spoils or gets dirty only when nobody watches it, and Torah is forgotten only through הסח הדעת, not paying attention.

keyTerms.meaning: taking one's mind off something; lack of attention

steps.whatToRemember: Torah is forgotten only through הסח הדעת. Steady attention and review keep it alive, the way watching a liquid keeps it from spoiling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for the value of constant review and focus in learning.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
just as these three liquids
phrases.notes: Water, wine and milk, which were mentioned earlier.

phrases.english: are spoiled only through lack of attention —
so too, words of Torah are not forgotten
except through lack of attention.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent reason for the same comparison of Torah to the three liquids.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah, like guarded liquids, is lost only through inattention.

steps.title: The day of rain is as great as the day of creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says the day of rain is as great as the day heaven and earth were created, and brings a פסוק from ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: The day of rain is as great as the day heaven and earth were created. As it says: 'Drip down, heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness; let the earth open and bring forth salvation, and let righteousness sprout together; I, ה׳, have created it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main topic, rain. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא makes a big claim and quotes a פסוק to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that a day of rain matches the day of creation in greatness. The פסוק describes rain from the heavens making the earth sprout, and ends with 'I, ה׳, have created it.' The exact proof from those last words comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Great is the day of rain
like the day on which heaven and earth were created,
as it says: 'Drip down, heavens, from above,'
and let the skies pour down righteousness;
let the earth open and let salvation bear fruit,
and let righteousness sprout together;
I, ה׳, have created it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא גָּדוֹל יוֹם הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the Torah-and-water story and returns to the main topic of rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The day of rain is as great as the day of creation.

steps.title: The proof comes from the singular word 'created it'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'בראתיו' (I created it), not 'בראתים' (I created them). This shows that rain is treated like an act of creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not say 'I created them' but 'I created it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the exact word in the פסוק that proves רבי חמא ברבי חנינא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק were talking about heaven and earth, it would say 'them' in the plural. Instead it says 'it' in the singular, meaning the rain. So the פסוק speaks of rain the way one speaks of creation.

keyTerms.meaning: it does not say this, but rather that (a formula for a precise reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'it' as heaven and earth. The proof depends on the singular word pointing to the rain.

phrases.english: It does not say 'I created them,'
but rather 'I created it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרָאתִים לֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶלָּא בְּרָאתִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 3 proves the claim.
steps.raayaObject: That the day of rain is like the day of creation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The singular word 'בראתיו' in ישעיה מה:ח, which points to the rain.

steps.title: On the day of rain, even salvation grows
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא says the day of rain is great because even salvation multiplies on it, from 'let the earth open and let salvation bear fruit.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: The day of rain is great, because even salvation is fruitful and multiplies on it. As it says: 'Let the earth open and let salvation bear fruit.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage praises the day of rain, using the same פסוק from ישעיה but a different phrase in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אושעיא focuses on the words 'ויפרו ישע.' On a day of rain, not only crops grow but also ישועה, salvation. Rain marks a time of ה׳'s favor.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
Great is the day of rain,
for even salvation is fruitful and multiplies on it,
as it says: 'Let the earth open and let salvation bear fruit.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא גָּדוֹל יוֹם הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another praise of the day of rain, drawn from a different phrase in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salvation increases on the day of rain.

steps.title: Rain falls only after Israel's sins are forgiven
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי says rain comes only when ישראל's sins have been forgiven, citing תהלים פ״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי said: Rain falls only if the sins of ישראל have been forgiven. As it says: 'ה׳, You have favored Your land; You have returned the captivity of יעקב. You have forgiven the sin of Your people; You have covered all their sins, Selah.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third sage ties rain to forgiveness. Rain is a sign that ה׳ has forgiven the people's sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links ה׳'s favor to the land with His forgiveness of the people. Later in that same chapter of תהלים, righteousness looks down from heaven, which is understood as rain. So rain depends on מחילת עוונות, the forgiveness of sins.

keyTerms.meaning: You favored, You were pleased with

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why droughts lead to fasting and תשובה, which is the central theme of מסכת תענית.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum bar Chanilai said:
The rains do not fall

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִמְחֲלוּ עֲוֹנוֹתֵיהֶן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: unless the sins of Israel have been forgiven,
as it says: 'ה׳, You have favored Your land;'
You have returned the captivity of Yaakov.
You have forgiven the sin of Your people;
You have covered all their sins, Selah.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בַּר חֲנִילַאי אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים יוֹרְדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of statements about rain, now linking it to forgiveness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain falls only after ישראל's sins are forgiven.

steps.title: A different verse for the same idea: rain and forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: זעירי מדיהבת tells רבינא that his community learns the link between rain and forgiveness from שלמה's prayer in מלכים, not from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי מדיהבת said to רבינא: You learn this from here, but we learn it from here: 'And You will hear in heaven and forgive the sin...'
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי מדיהבת tells רבינא that his community uses a different פסוק as the source for רבי תנחום בר חנילאי's idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that rain depends on forgiveness. They only differ on which פסוק teaches it. זעירי's source is שלמה's prayer: ה׳ hears from heaven, forgives the sin, and then sends rain on the land.
steps.whatToRemember: Rain is connected to forgiveness of sin. One tradition learns this from תהלים פ״ה, another from שלמה's prayer in מלכים א׳ ח׳.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a disagreement about the law. Both sides hold the same idea and only bring different פסוקים for it.

phrases.english: Ze'iri of Dihavat said to Ravina:
You learn it from here.
We learn it from here:
'And You will hear in heaven
and forgive the sin, etc.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א׳ ח:לו. The פסוק goes on to say 'and send rain upon Your land.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן מֵהָכָא מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ אֲנַן מֵהָכָא מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the idea in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That rain depends on forgiveness of ישראל's sins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שלמה's prayer in מלכים א׳ ח:לה-לו, where forgiveness comes before the sending of rain.

steps.title: Rain stops only when ישראל deserve destruction
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום בריה דרבי חייא says rain is held back only when ישראל are guilty enough to deserve destruction, based on a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום בריה דרבי חייא, from כפר עכו, said: The rains are held back only if the enemies of ישראל (meaning ישראל itself) have become liable for destruction. As it says: 'Drought and heat steal the snow waters; the grave, those who sinned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the reverse of the earlier steps: what makes rain stop. רבי תנחום says it happens only when ישראל's sins have reached a very serious level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said rain comes when sins are forgiven. Here the other side is stated: rain stops when sins are so great that the people deserve destruction. The פסוק links the 'stealing' of snow waters to 'those who sinned' who deserve the grave.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the enemies of Israel', a polite way of saying Israel itself

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'שונאיהן של ישראל' does NOT mean the real enemies of ישראל. It is a polite way of speaking, used so as not to say something bad directly about ישראל. It means ישראל themselves.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum, son of Rabbi Chiya, said
a man of the village of Akko:
The rains are not held back
unless they have become liable,
the enemies of Israel, for destruction,
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying Israel itself.

phrases.english: as it says: 'Drought and also heat
will steal the snow waters;
the grave, those who sinned.'
phrases.notes: איוב 24:19. Those who sinned deserve the grave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from what brings rain (forgiveness) to what holds it back (serious guilt).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is held back only when ישראל have become liable for destruction.

steps.title: זעירי gives a different source from the תורה
steps.stepSummary: זעירי מדיהבת tells רבינא that his community learns the same idea from a פסוק in דברים: 'He will close the heavens, and you will perish quickly.'
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי מדיהבת said to רבינא: You learn it from here. We learn it from here: 'And He will close up the heavens... and you will perish quickly.'
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי agrees with the idea of רבי תנחום but offers a different, clearer פסוק as its source, just as he did in Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים places 'closing the heavens' (no rain) right next to 'you will perish quickly' (destruction). This shows plainly that stopping rain is tied to deserving destruction. The ruling does not change; only the source changes.

keyTerms.meaning: and He will close up the heavens

phrases.english: Ze'iri of Dihavat said to Ravina:
You, from here you learn it.
We, from here we learn it:
'And He will close up the heavens
and you will perish quickly.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ זְעֵירִי מִדִּיהֲבַת לְרָבִינָא: אַתּוּן, מֵהָכָא מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another source for the same idea as Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That rain is withheld when ישראל deserve destruction.

steps.title: Rain stops because people fail to separate תרומות ומעשרות
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says rain is held back because people neglect תרומות ומעשרות, using the same פסוק from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The rains are held back only because of the neglect of תרומות ומעשרות, as it says: 'Drought and heat steal the snow waters.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא names a specific sin that causes rain to stop: not separating תרומות ומעשרות. He uses the same פסוק that רבי תנחום used in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי תנחום used the end of the פסוק ('those who sinned'). רב חסדא uses the beginning ('drought and heat') to point to one specific sin. It is not yet clear how these words hint at תרומות ומעשרות, which sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the portions of produce that must be given to the כהן, the לוי, and others

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: The rains are not held back
except because of the neglect of terumot and maasrot,
as it says: 'Drought and also heat
will steal the snow waters.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל בִּיטּוּל תְּרוּמוֹת וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second cause for withheld rain, using the same פסוק as Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is held back because of the neglect of תרומות ומעשרות.

steps.title: How does the פסוק show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the פסוק the hint to תרומות ומעשרות can be found.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: how do the words 'drought and heat' teach anything about תרומות ומעשרות? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not mention תרומות ומעשרות at all, so the link needs to be explained. This is a real request for explanation, not an attack on רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: from where is it implied? / how does this show it?

phrases.english: From where is this implied?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רב חסדא's פסוק supports his claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How 'צִיָּה גַם חֹם' points to תרומות ומעשרות.

steps.title: Summer duties neglected cause winter rain to be taken away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל explains: commandments given for the hot season that were not done cause the rain to be taken away in the rainy season.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Because of the things I commanded you to do in the hot season and you did not do them, the snow waters will be stolen from you in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל. 'חֹם' (heat) points to summer duties, which are not kept, and as a result the rain is lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The harvest is in the hot season, and that is when תרומות ומעשרות must be separated. If people do not do it then, the 'snow waters' are taken from them in winter. This is how the פסוק's 'heat' is tied to the sin רב חסדא named.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: Not separating תרומות ומעשרות at harvest time (summer) causes the rain to be lost in winter. The punishment matches the sin: holding back from the produce leads to the produce's rain being held back.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Because of things that I commanded you
in the hot season, and you did not do them —
phrases.notes: Such as separating תרומות ומעשרות from the summer harvest.

phrases.english: the snow waters will be stolen from you
in the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'חֹם' means duties of the hot season (תרומות ומעשרות). Failing to do them causes the 'snow waters' to be taken away in winter.

steps.title: Rain stops because of people who speak לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן פזי says rain is held back because of those who speak לשון הרע, from a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said: The rains are held back only because of those who speak לשון הרע, as it says: 'The north wind brings forth rain, and an angry face, a secret tongue.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא names a different cause for rain stopping: לשון הרע. He brings a פסוק that links rain to a 'hidden tongue'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places 'rain' next to 'an angry face' and 'a secret tongue', meaning gossip spoken behind someone's back. The idea is that when people speak לשון הרע, the heavens show an 'angry face' and hold back the rain.

keyTerms.meaning: those who speak לשון הרע (harmful talk about others)
a secret tongue, talk behind someone's back

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said:
The rains are not held back
except because of those who speak lashon hara,
as it says: 'The north wind brings forth rain,
and an angry face, a secret tongue.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל מְסַפְּרֵי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another cause to the list of reasons rain is withheld.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is held back because of those who speak לשון הרע.

steps.title: Rain stops because of brazen people
steps.stepSummary: רב סלא in the name of רב המנונא says rain is held back because of עזי פנים, from a פסוק in ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סלא said in the name of רב המנונא: The rains are held back only because of brazen people, as it says: 'The showers were withheld, and there was no late rain, yet you had the forehead of a harlot...'
steps.whatsHappening: One more cause is added: being brazen and shameless. The פסוק directly connects the lack of rain to a 'harlot's forehead', meaning shamelessness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק, 'showers withheld' and 'no late rain' appear right beside 'a harlot's forehead'. A brazen forehead stands for someone who feels no shame. So shamelessness is shown as a cause of rain being held back.

keyTerms.meaning: the late rain (at the end of the rainy season)
the forehead of a harlot, a picture of shamelessness

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Salla said in the name of Rav Hamnuna:
The rains are not held back
except because of brazen people,
as it says: 'And the showers were withheld,
and there was no late rain,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵצַח אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה הָיָה לָךְ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and you had the forehead of a harlot, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל עַזֵּי פָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another cause to the list of reasons rain is withheld.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is held back because of עזי פנים.

steps.title: A brazen person will end up sinning
steps.stepSummary: רב סלא in the name of רב המנונא adds, from the same פסוק, that anyone who is brazen will eventually stumble into sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב סלא said in the name of רב המנונא: Any person who is brazen will in the end stumble into sin, as it says: 'And you had the forehead of a harlot.'
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same פסוק, the same teachers make a second point: brazenness leads a person to sin in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'harlot's forehead' is read as a warning about the future. A person with no shame will eventually fall into serious sin, the kind connected to a 'harlot'. This sets up רב נחמן's different reading in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Salla said in the name of Rav Hamnuna:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עַזּוּת פָּנִים —
phrases.english: Any person who has brazenness —
will in the end stumble into sin,
as it says: 'And you had the forehead of a harlot.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עַזּוּת פָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching by the same teachers, drawn from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brazen person will eventually stumble into sin.

steps.title: רב נחמן: it is known that he already sinned
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reads the פסוק differently: since it says 'you had' (past tense), a brazen person has surely already sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It is known that he has already stumbled into sin, as it says: 'you had', and it does not say 'you will have'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן disagrees about the time in the פסוק. He says brazenness does not only lead to sin later; it shows that the person has already sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב סלא read the פסוק as a warning about the future ('will in the end stumble'). רב נחמן points to the exact word: 'היה' (was) is past tense, not 'יהיה' (will be). So brazenness is a sign of a sin that already happened.

keyTerms.meaning: it is known, it is certain

steps.whatToRemember: Two views on brazenness: רב סלא says a brazen person will end up sinning in the future. רב נחמן says, from the past tense 'היה', that he has surely already sinned.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
It is known that he has already stumbled into sin,
as it says: 'you had',
and it does not say 'you will have'.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁנִּכְשַׁל בַּעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with Step 15 on whether the פסוק speaks about future sin or past sin.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the future-tense reading ('סוף נכשל'). Accepts the link between brazenness and sin.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק uses the past tense 'היה', not the future 'יהיה'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brazen person has certainly already stumbled into sin, as shown by the past tense 'היה לך'.

steps.title: A brazen person may be called wicked
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that a person with עזות פנים may be called a רשע, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Any person who is brazen may be called wicked, as it says: 'A wicked man makes his face brazen.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps talking about the brazen person from the previous steps. רבה בר רב הונא adds a practical rule: you may call such a person a רשע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links 'רשע' directly to a brazen face ('הֵעֵז... בְּפָנָיו'). So brazenness is treated as a sign of wickedness, and labeling him that way is allowed. This is a new statement with its own פסוק, continuing the topic of the brazen person.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עַזּוּת פָּנִים —
phrases.english: Any person who has brazenness of face —
it is permitted to call him wicked,
as it is said: 'A wicked man makes his face brazen.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the brazen person and adds a practical consequence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is permitted to call a brazen person a רשע.

steps.title: A brazen person may even be hated
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק goes further: it is permitted to hate a brazen person, reading a פסוק in קהלת with an אל תקרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is permitted to hate him, as it says: 'And the brazenness of his face is changed.' Do not read 'is changed' (יְשֻׁנֶּא), but 'is hated' (יִשָּׂנֵא).
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a stronger rule about the brazen person: not only may you call him wicked, you may even hate him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses an אל תקרי, which is a rereading of the same letters with different vowels. 'יְשֻׁנֶּא' (is changed) is reread as 'יִשָּׂנֵא' (is hated). The plain meaning of the פסוק is not removed. The rereading adds an extra lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as... but rather as (a rereading of the same letters)

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the פסוק is spelled wrong or that its simple meaning is cancelled. It reads an additional lesson into the same letters.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
it is permitted to hate him,
as it is said: 'And the brazenness of his face is changed.'
Do not read 'is changed,' but rather 'is hated.'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Could be seen as a parallel or stronger opinion to step 17 rather than a disagreement.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stronger consequence for the brazen person than step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is permitted to hate a brazen person.
steps.whatToRemember: The brazen-person section ends here: such a person may be called a רשע (step 17) and may even be hated (step 18).

steps.title: Rain is held back because of neglect of Torah study
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא says rain is withheld only because of ביטול תורה. He reads a פסוק in קהלת and defines its words 'מך' and 'מקרה' from other פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: Rain is held back only because of neglect of Torah, as it says: 'Through laziness the rafters sink.' Because of the laziness among ישראל, who did not occupy themselves with Torah, 'the enemy of הקדוש ברוך הוא' (a respectful way of saying God Himself) became 'poor.' 'מך' means poor, as it says: 'If he is too poor for your valuation.' And 'מקרה' means הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says: 'Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main topic of why rain is held back. רב קטינא names a new cause: ביטול תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק says that laziness makes a house's rafters sag. רב קטינא rereads it in three parts. The 'laziness' is laziness in Torah study. 'מך' means poor, from ויקרא. 'מקרה' refers to God, the one who 'lays beams in the water,' from תהלים. So when ישראל neglects Torah, God, so to speak, becomes 'poor' and holds back the rain.

keyTerms.meaning: Rain is held back only because of...
'The enemy of God': a respectful way of referring to God Himself
Rafters or beams; here read as referring to God

steps.confusionAlert: 'שׂוֹנְאוֹ שֶׁל הקב"ה' does not mean an actual enemy of God. It is a respectful way of avoiding saying something negative directly about God.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said:
The rains are not held back
except because of neglect of Torah,
as it is said: 'Through laziness the rafters sink' —
because of the laziness that was in Israel
that they did not occupy themselves with Torah —

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשֶׂה שׂוֹנְאוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָךְ.
phrases.english: the 'enemy' of the Holy One, Blessed be He, became poor.
phrases.notes: A respectful way of referring to God Himself

phrases.english: And 'מך' means nothing but poor,
as it is said: 'And if he is too poor for your valuation.'
And 'מקרה' refers to none other than the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is said: 'Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the water.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the brazen-person topic and returns to the list of sins that hold back rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is held back because of ביטול תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It adds Torah study to the list of causes of drought, alongside לשון הרע (step 13) and עזות פנים (step 14).

steps.title: A different verse for the same idea: Torah is 'light'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a different source for the same idea (ביטול תורה holds back rain), from a פסוק in איוב, defining 'אור' as Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: From here: 'And now they do not see the light; it is bright in the skies, and a wind passes and clears them.' 'Light' means Torah, as it says: 'For a מצוה is a lamp and Torah is light.' So when people do not 'see the light' of Torah, 'it is bright in the skies,' meaning there are no rain clouds.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף agrees that ביטול תורה holds back rain, but he proves it from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מֵהָכָא' (from here) signals a new source for the same idea, not a disagreement. 'Not seeing light' means not learning Torah, since משלי calls Torah 'light.' The result is that 'it is bright in the skies,' meaning clear skies with no clouds, so no rain.

keyTerms.meaning: From here (introduces a different source for the same idea)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: From here:
'And now they do not see the light;'
'it is bright in the skies,'
'and a wind passes and clears them.'
And 'light' means nothing but Torah,
as it is said: 'For a מצוה is a lamp and Torah is light' —
'it is bright in the skies' (meaning no rain clouds).

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה: an additional proof for רב קטינא's idea
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative פסוק for the same idea as step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ביטול תורה holds back rain, derived from איוב: when Torah ('light') is not seen, the skies stay clear.

steps.title: Even rain clouds get blown away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל explains the end of רב יוסף's פסוק: even when the sky is full of rain clouds, a wind comes and clears them away.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Even when the sky is full of bright clouds ready to bring down dew and rain, 'a wind passes and clears them,' and no rain falls.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains the last part of the פסוק that רב יוסף just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף explained 'it is bright in the skies' as clear skies. This ברייתא adds a further point: even when clouds have already formed and rain seems about to fall, a wind blows them away. Rain can be lost even at the last moment.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael:
Even at a time when the sky becomes
full of bright clouds,
ready to bring down dew and rain —
'a wind passes and clears them.'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תשובה: an explanation of the end of the פסוק
steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the פסוק quoted in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when rain clouds are ready, a wind can clear them away because of ביטול תורה.

steps.title: Rain is held back because of robbery
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says rain is withheld only because of גזל. He reads a פסוק in איוב and defines 'כפים' as violence and 'אור' as rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Rain is held back only because of the sin of robbery, as it says: 'Because of hands, He covers the light.' Because of the sin of the hands, He covered the light. 'Hands' means violence, as it says: 'And from the violence that is in their hands.' And 'light' means rain, as it says: 'He spreads the cloud of His light.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives a new cause for rain being held back: גזל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי reads 'עַל כַּפַּיִם' as 'because of the sin of the hands.' He proves from יונה that 'hands' refers to stealing (חמס). He proves from איוב that 'light' here means rain. So the פסוק says: because of robbery, God covers (holds back) the rain.

keyTerms.meaning: Hands; here read as stealing done with the hands

steps.confusionAlert: In step 20, 'אור' meant Torah. Here, in a different פסוק, 'אור' means rain. The same word is read differently depending on its context.
steps.whatToRemember: The list of sins that hold back rain keeps growing: unfulfilled מצוות of the summer, לשון הרע, עזות פנים, ביטול תורה, and now גזל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
The rains are not held back
except because of the sin of robbery,
as it is said: 'Because of hands, He covers the light.'
Because of the sin of the hands — He covered the light.
And 'hands' means nothing but violence (robbery),
as it is said: 'And from the violence that is in their hands,'
and 'light' means nothing but rain,
as it is said: 'He spreads the cloud of His light.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another sin to the list of causes of drought, using the same 'אין הגשמים נעצרין אלא' formula as step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is held back because of גזל.

steps.title: The fix for rain held back because of stealing: pray more
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רבי אמי's teaching about גזל, the גמרא asks what the fix is. The answer is to increase prayer. This is learned from 'בְּמַפְגִּיעַ' in איוב, and פגיעה is shown to mean prayer from a פסוק in ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his fix? He should pray more. As it says: 'And He commanded it because of one who implores' (איוב). And 'imploring' (פגיעה) means only prayer, as it says: 'And you, do not pray for this nation… and do not implore Me' (ירמיה).
steps.whatsHappening: Step 22 said rain is held back because of גזל. Now the גמרא gives the fix: pray a lot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the very next part of the same פסוק in איוב that רבי אמי used in Step 22. The word 'בְּמַפְגִּיעַ' is decoded with a second פסוק. In ירמיה, 'אַל תִּפְגַּע בִּי' sits right next to 'אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל', so פגיעה must mean prayer.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read פגיעה as 'hitting' or 'meeting' here. The גמרא proves from ירמיה that in this context it means prayer.

phrases.english: What is his fix?
phrases.notes: Refers to the person whose stealing caused rain to be held back (Step 22).

phrases.english: He should increase his prayer,
as it says: 'And He commanded it because of one who implores' (Job 36:32),
phrases.notes: The continuation of the same פסוק used in Step 22.

phrases.english: and 'imploring' means nothing other than prayer,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתָּה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל בְּעַד הָעָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: as it says: 'And you, do not pray for this nation'
etc. 'and do not implore Me' (Jeremiah 7:16).
phrases.notes: Since 'implore' appears beside 'pray', the two mean the same thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remedy for the problem raised in Step 22 (rain withheld because of גזל), using the same פסוק in איוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fix for rain withheld because of גזל is to increase prayer.

steps.title: A sky 'blunt like iron' comes from a corrupt generation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי reads the פסוק in קהלת 'אם קהה הברזל'. A sky that is hard like iron and gives no dew or rain is caused by the generation's corrupt deeds, based on the word 'קלקל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אמי said: What does it mean when it says, 'If the iron is blunt, and he does not sharpen the edge'? If you see a sky that has become hard like iron and does not bring down dew and rain, it is because of the deeds of the generation, which are corrupt. As it says: 'and he did not sharpen (קלקל) the face (פנים).'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives a second teaching about rain. A sky that stays 'iron-hard' and gives no rain is a sign that the generation's behavior is ruined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'iron' in the פסוק is read as the sky, which can become hard and stop giving rain. The word 'קלקל' is read like 'מקולקלין', meaning corrupt, and 'פנים' (face) hints at the people of the generation. So the cause of drought is broader here than the single sin of Step 22: it is the generation's overall corruption.

keyTerms.meaning: blunt, dulled (here: a hard, closed-up sky)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'If the iron is blunt,'
'and he does not sharpen the edge' (Ecclesiastes 10:10)?
If you see a sky that has become hard like iron
so that it does not bring down dew and rain,
it is because of the deeds of the generation
which are corrupt,
as it says: 'and he did not sharpen the edge.'
phrases.notes: קלקל is read as 'corrupt', and פנים (face) as the generation or its leaders.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same רבי אמי about the cause of drought, now from a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the sky withholds dew and rain, it is because the generation's deeds are corrupt.

steps.title: The fix: pour out prayers for mercy, though right behavior from the start is better
steps.stepSummary: The fix for a corrupt generation is to strengthen themselves in prayers for mercy, based on 'וחילים יגבר'. The end of the פסוק teaches that it would have been even better if their deeds had been proper from the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is their fix? They should strengthen themselves in prayer for mercy, as it says: 'Then he must increase his strength, and wisdom is an advantage to make things right.' All the more so if their deeds had been made right from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the same פסוק, רבי אמי gives the fix: the people must pray hard for mercy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וחילים יגבר' (increase strength) is read as putting real strength into prayers for mercy. 'ויתרון הכשיר חכמה' is read as a קל וחומר: if prayer after the fact helps, then deeds that were proper from the start would have helped even more.

keyTerms.meaning: they should strengthen themselves in prayers for mercy
to make proper, to set right

steps.whatToRemember: Two teachings of רבי אמי share one pattern. First a sin is named that causes drought (גזל, or general corruption). Then a fix is given from the same פסוק: prayer, or strong prayer for mercy.

phrases.english: What is their fix?
They should strengthen themselves in prayers for mercy,
as it says: 'Then he must increase his strength,'
'and wisdom is an advantage to make things right' (Ecclesiastes 10:10),

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אִם הוּכְשְׁרוּ מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן מֵעִיקָּרָא.
phrases.english: all the more so if their deeds had been made right from the beginning.
phrases.notes: Better to behave properly from the start than to need the fix later.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה תַּקָּנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remedy for the corruption described in Step 24, from the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A corrupt generation should strengthen itself in prayers for mercy. Proper deeds from the start are even better.

steps.title: ריש לקיש begins a different reading of the same verse
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש opens a new reading of 'אם קהה הברזל', this time about a תלמיד. This passage ends in the middle of his statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: If you see a student…
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a second, different explanation of the same פסוק in קהלת, and the rest of ריש לקיש's words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the 'iron' was the sky. ריש לקיש is about to apply the same image to a תלמיד and his learning, so the topic shifts from rain to Torah study.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא רבי שמעון בן לקיש

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
If you see a student
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אִם רָאִיתָ תַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different interpretation of the פסוק that רבי אמי explained in Steps 24 and 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: (Incomplete on this amud.) ריש לקיש applies 'אם קהה הברזל' to a תלמיד.
